newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Gauteng racing industry to list in 1997.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Gauteng racing industry to list in 1997.

text.p: The horse-racing industry in South Africa's Gauteng province will seek a listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange next year as part of the privatisation of the region's operations, officials said On Friday.

"Based on a rough guideline we should conclude negotiations with the provincial government by the end of the year," Tony Wintour, financial executive of the Highveld Racing Authority (HRA), told Reuters.
"Agreement must then be reached with club members which will take us into early next year. It will take about six months after that to get a listing."
The racing industry, which commands betting turnover of 1.3 billion rand a year, has until now been tightly controlled and heavily taxed by the provincial government.
Wintour said the two parties had by mutual consent decided to part ways. "Both feel the industry must run its own business."
Legislation passed in June also prohibits government from involvement in gambling activities.
Wintour said the listing was partly a cash-raising exercise, but was also aimed at streamlining the industry and bringing a black empowerment group on board as a stakeholder.
He said before the listing could take place the industry needed to negotiate a reduced tax rate with the provincial government in order to compete with other forms of gaming.
Until the passing of the National Gambling Act on June 18, horse-racing constituted the only legal form of gambling in South Africa.
Members of the HRA this week voted in favour of the privatisation of all racing operations in Gauteng, the densely-populated province around Johannesburg.
An earlier proposal would have seen the gambling operations, Betco, listed first and after two years buying the racing arm, Racing Inc.

Gauteng's racing industry controls some 300-400 million rand of racing assets. The primary assets include three clubs -- the Gosforth Park Turf Club, the Newmarket Turf Club and the Turfontein Race Club -- and the Totalizator Agency Board.
